results.title: Reducing Import Costs for High-Value Components in the Battery & Energy Storage Supply Chain — RK Logistics
results.content:
Consider a typical shipment of 18650 cells destined for U.S. EV assembly lines. At $50,000 per pallet, a 7.5% MFN duty plus 25% Section 301 tariffs adds $16,250 in costs—before value-added tax or bonding fees. Multiply by quarterly volumes, and you’re staring at seven-figure exposures annually. [...] High-value components like lithium-ion cells, electrolytes, and anode materials drive the battery and energy storage (BES) supply chain, but soaring import duties can erode margins. Tariffs under Section 301 on Chinese-origin goods often exceed 25%, compounded by anti-dumping measures on solar-grade polysilicon. Precision in logistics strategy turns these headwinds into tailwinds through duty mitigation tactics.

## The Hidden Duty Burden on BES Imports [...] Privilege Status: Pay duties on imported status, not finished goods—ideal for subassemblies entering FTZs for kitting or light manufacturing.
 Inverted Tariff Savings: Assemble imported cells with domestic packs; pay lower duties on batteries (HTS 8507) versus raw cells (8507.60).
 Scrap and Waste Relief: Defective materials destroyed in-zone incur no duties, streamlining reverse logistics.

results.title: Tariffs and Trade Risk in Energy Storage Projects: 2026 Outlook
results.content: Tariffs and supply chain integrity remain top-of-mind trade concerns for energy storage projects. The US administration has imposed sweeping tariff regimes and pursued remedies specifically affecting industries critical to energy storage, which have had a significant impact on project development. Within this everchanging environment, companies can take steps in developing their project documents and supply chain strategy to positively position themselves  to proactively address trade concerns [...] In the context of engineering, procurement, and construction (EPC) contracts and equipment supply agreements, mitigating the risks associated with tariff and duties changes for imported goods is critical in ensuring the financial stability and timely completion of the project. [...] Storage batteries have been indicated as a priority for border detentions for forced labor evaluation, and we expect to continue seeing those goods identified as a concern. It will be key for companies to understand their supply chain for materials and finished goods and be prepared to respond quickly should US Customs and Border Protection (CBP) issue a questionnaire regarding the use of forced labor in the production of imported merchandise.
